mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 4%) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a recovery in manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% combined with a concurrent acceleration in average hourly earnings (not available, so use PAYEMS as a proxy for labor market tightness) above 0.4% monthly for two months signals labor market overheating, which precedes wage inflation and higher input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS > 0.4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1,000 thousand units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.4% after a period of stable inflation (previous three months < 0.2%) signals a breakout in price pressures, which increases the likelihood of future Fed tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.3% in the same month signals a significant labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month +0.3% AND PAYEMS < previous month -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals weak macroeconomic demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
